passages.c: The microclimate of the urban garden and its associated ecosystem is an ideal setting for the study of microbiology. The microfauna of the soil is diverse, however only evident under a powerful microscope. The microorganisms such as bacteria and fungus spores are microscopic, some less than a micron in length. However, each of these microorganisms perform a vital role in the health of the garden soil. The soil's microfauna are the decomposers of the garden ecosystem and have a vital role in recycling nutrients. However, care must be taken when studying soil as some harmful microbes may be present, which can cause serious illness if inhaled or ingested.

passages.c: After thoughtful consideration, I have determined that whether one is joyful or resentful is a matter of perspective. When we focus on the dreadful things that happen, the awful misfortune or the armful of chores to be completed, we find ourselves resentful and miserable. However, we have a choice instead to see the spoonful of sugar in all of our daily tasks. When we choose a cheerful attitude and focus on the beautiful things all around us, we find ourselves hopeful. We must be careful however that we are honest. It is doubtful anyone can have a wonderful day every day. It is possible though to choose a joyful heart and a hopeful attitude even when dreadful things happen.

passages.c: The baker rises early to bake bread. The plumber spends all day repairing toilets. The builder requires approval from the engineer to construct buildings and dwellings. The butcher prepares the sausages and the cashier takes the money. The soldier fights to keep the country free and the reporter researches stories for the newspaper. The painter dedicates his life to creating a masterpiece. But the teacher rises early to plan learning experiences, then she devotes all day to developing her students' abilities. The teacher requires approval from the principal for the concert. She prepares the recital and presents all the awards. The teacher is committed to her students' study, and then she composes reports to show all they have learnt. The teacher dedicates her life to educating students!

The solicitor contributed his prizewinning strawberry shortcake he had entered as a competitor at the local fair. The conductor and his wife, the auditor, bought along some homemade lemonade. And the elderly lady from number 4 served tea on her silver tray. She was a collector of antiques and an instructor in the art of calligraphy. passages.c: It began as a harmless prank. Restless from being cooped up all day, the fatherless children wandered around the lobby. Perhaps they were a little careless as they giggled and dashed past the priceless antique vase, but as the vase crashed to the floor they stood helpless. The manager of the hotel was merciless in his accusations, declaring them reckless, worthless tramps. A childless couple witnessed the exchange and came to the children's defence. The gentleman calmly reminded the manager it was pointless to demand retribution for a priceless article and observed the children had only been a little careless. But when the gentleman explained it was really the manager's fault for carelessly putting the vase in such a precarious location, the manager was speechless.

passages.c: The pessimist artist sees the world as shades of grey, but the optimist artist sees the world in vibrant colour. The pessimist pianist plays mournful tunes, but the optimist pianist plays a jolly jig. The pessimist cyclist says the world has too many cars, but the optimist cyclist notices all the new riders on the road. The pessimist journalist writes stories of doom and gloom, but the optimist journalist writes of overcoming the odds. The pessimist scientist says we are headed for the end, but the optimist scientist sees the wonder in creation. What will you be, a pessimist who sees the glass half empty or an optimist who sees the glass half full?
